'''Geert Jan van Oldenborgh''' (22 October 1961 – 12 October 2021) was a Dutch climatologist and physicist.<ref>{{Cite news |date=14 October 2021 |title=Dutch Climate Scientist Geert Jan Van Oldenborgh Dies At 59 |language=en |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-10-14/dutch-climate-scientist-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-dies-at-59|access-date=22 October 2021}}</ref><ref name=auto>{{Cite web |date=14 October 2021|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2401595-internationaal-gelauwerde-klimaatexpert-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-overleden |title=Internationaal gelauwerde klimaatexpert Geert Jan van Oldenborgh overleden |trans-title=Internationally acclaimed climate expert Geert Jan van Oldenborgh has passed away |publisher=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting]]|access-date=15 October 2021|archive-date=14 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211014054607/https://nos.nl/artikel/2401595-internationaal-gelauwerde-klimaatexpert-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-overleden|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |url=https://www.nu.nl/klimaat/6162220/baanbrekende-klimaatonderzoeker-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-59-overleden.html |title=Baanbrekende klimaatonderzoeker Geert Jan van |archive-date=14 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211014001217/https://www.nu.nl/klimaat/6162220/baanbrekende-klimaatonderzoeker-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-59-overleden.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=auto3>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2021/10/14/klimaatwetenschapper-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-59-overleden-a4061818 |title=Klimaatwetenschapper Geert Jan van Oldenborgh (59) overleden |trans-title=Climate scientist Geert Jan van Oldenborgh (59) has passed away |work=[[NRC Handelsblad]] |access-date=15 October 2021 |archive-date=14 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211014054631/https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2021/10/14/klimaatwetenschapper-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-59-overleden-a4061818 |url-status=live}}</ref> Through his career he studied climate modelling of adverse weather events and was known as a pioneer of [[attribution science]], driving public awareness of how climate change is linked to extreme weather events. He was also the creator of a digital platform, ''Climate Explorer'', an online meteorological data repository and platform for climate data analysis.

He was a recipient of the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]] in 2021. He was also named by [[Time (magazine)|''Time'']] as one of the 100 most influential people of 2021.

== Early life ==
Geert Jan van Oldenborgh was born on 22 October 1961 in [[Rotterdam]] to Jan van Oldenborgh and Wil Lijbrink. His father was a lawyer while his mother was a [[Psychoanalysis|psychoanalyst]].<ref name="nytobit">{{Cite news |last=Fountain|first=Henry |date=22 October 2021 |title=Geert Jan van Oldenborgh, 59, Dies; Linked Weather Disasters to Climate Change|language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/22/climate/geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-dead.html |access-date=22 October 2021 |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=22 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022192106/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/22/climate/geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-dead.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2 November 2021 |title=Geert Jan van Oldenborgh obituary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2021/nov/02/geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-obituary |access-date=3 November 2021 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref> While in school in the Netherlands, he received a scholarship to go to [[Lester B. Pearson College]] in [[Victoria, British Columbia]], in Canada. During his time there, he studied Chinese. He obtained his master's degree in [[theoretical physics]] from [[Leiden University]] in the Netherlands in 1986. He also studied mathematics and Chinese in the university. He completed his [[PhD]] from the [[University of Amsterdam]] and the [[Nikhef|Netherlands Institute of Nuclear and High Energy Physics]] in 1990.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Van Oldenborgh started his teaching and research career at [[LMU Munich]] and the [[Paul Scherrer Institute]] in Switzerland, where he studied [[Elementary particle|elementary particles]] before returning to Leiden in 1994.<ref name=":0" /> He worked at the [[Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute]] (KNMI) from 1996, and as a professor at [[Oxford University]] from 2019.<ref name=":0" /> 

During his time at the KNMI, he focused on ways to improve forecast accuracy while studying [[El Niño]], the weather phenomenon in the Pacific Ocean which recurs every few years and upsets global weather patterns.<ref name=":0" /> He also created the digital platform, ''Climate Explorer'', that serves as a digital repository of vast troves of climate-linked data including global temperature measurements, ozone levels, sea ice levels, rainfall measurements, ocean temperatures, and historical records of cyclones, hurricanes and droughts. Some of the data in the platform goes back to the fourteenth century.<ref name=":0" /> His work on the digital platform won him the technology achievement award from the [[European Meteorological Society]].<ref name=":0" />

=== Event attribution ===
Over his career he authored over 150 [[Peer review|peer reviewed]] papers across multiple weather forecasting topics including [[seasonal forecasting]], [[Climate model|climate modelling]], and [[Extreme event attribution|event attribution]].<ref name=":0" /> He was known as a pioneer of [[attribution science]], which has been instrumental in driving public awareness of how climate change is linked to extreme weather.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 October 2021 |title=Pioneer of attribution science Geert Jan van Oldenborgh dies, aged 59 |url=https://www.climatechangenews.com/2021/10/15/pioneer-attribution-science-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-dies-aged-59/ |access-date=3 November 2021 |website=Climate Home News |language=en}}</ref> Together with the German climate researcher [[Friederike Otto]], he developed a method to determine the role of climate change shortly after major weather disasters. This led to the establishment of [[World Weather Attribution]], an international network of climate scientists and institutes.<ref name="auto" /><ref name="auto2" /><ref name="auto3" />  Along with other scientists, Van Oldenborgh contributed to studying linkages between [[climate change]] induced by human actions and catastrophic events such as droughts, floods, forest fires, and heatwaves.<ref name=":0" /> Some of the events that he and his fellow researchers identified as caused or accentuated by human-induced climate change included the [[2018 Sweden wildfires|2018 Swedish wildfires]], [[Australian bushfires]], [[2019 European heat waves]], [[2021 Siberia wildfires|2021 Siberian wildfires]], and the [[2021 European floods|2021 European floods across Germany and Belgium]].<ref name=":0" /> One of the group's studies of the [[2021 Pacific Northwest heat wave]], which spread across the west coast of the United States and Canada, found that the events were directly linked to climate change.<ref name="nytobit" /> Prior to Van Oldenborgh and other researchers' work on event attribution, the general view among scientists was that individual events could not be attributed to climate change. Work led by Van Oldenborgh and his peers proved that they could.<ref name="nytobit" />

His efforts were also instrumental in performing some of the attributional analyses when the events were fresh in people's minds, this required that the process be shortened by using models that had already been run rather than running models from scratch, a process that he described as 'precooking'.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fountain|first=Henry |date=1 August 2016 |title=Looking, Quickly, for the Fingerprints of Climate Change |language=en-US|work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/08/02/science/looking-quickly-for-the-fingerprints-of-climate-change.html |access-date=3 November 2021 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Some of their studies were also released prior to a [[peer review]], with the argument that the basic models and techniques had already been peer-reviewed and published in scientific journals.<ref name="nytobit" />

Van Oldenborgh contributed to the 2013 global report of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]].<ref name=":0" />

For his works he received in 2021 the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]] and the [[Europese Technology Achievement Award]]. In September 2021, [[Time (magazine)|''Time'']] named him one of the 100 most influential people of 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.kobr.nl/nieuws/human-interest/27776/klimaatonderzoeker-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-dubbel-geeerd |title=Klimaatonderzoeker Geert Jan van Oldenborgh dubbel geëerd |trans-title=Climate researcher Geert Jan van Oldenborgh double honoured |website=www.kobr.nl |access-date=15 October 2021 |archive-date=14 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514054717/https://www.kobr.nl/nieuws/human-interest/27776/klimaatonderzoeker-geert-jan-van-oldenborgh-dubbel-geeerd |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| last = Naber| first = Caspar| title = Time top 100: Nederlandse klimaatadvocaat Cox bij meest invloedrijke personen van 2021| work = [[Algemeen Dagblad]]| access-date = 2023-11-06| date = 2021-09-15| url = https://www.ad.nl/buitenland/time-top-100-nederlandse-klimaatadvocaat-cox-bij-meest-invloedrijke-personen-van-2021~ad751dea/ |trans-title=Time top 100: Dutch climate lawyer Cox among the most influential people of 2021 |
language = nl}}</ref><ref name="auto" /><ref name="auto2" /><ref name="auto3" />

== Personal life ==
Van Oldenborgh met his future wife, Mandy, a [[Clinical psychology|clinical psychologist]] and [[psychotherapist]] in 1982. The couple married in 1987 and went on to have three sons.<ref name=":0" />

In 2013, Van Oldenborgh was diagnosed with [[multiple myeloma]], also known as [[Kahler's disease]], a form of blood cancer.<ref name=":0" /> The blood cancer progressed in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.trouw.nl/gs-b2c6f980 |title=Van Oldenborgh maakt zich geen zorgen over zijn ziekte, wél over het klimaat: 'Ik zal nooit weten hoe dit afloopt' |trans-title=Van Oldenborgh is not worried about his illness, but he is concerned about the climate: 'I will never know how this will end' |first=Joep|last=Engels |date=4 January 2020 |website=Trouw |access-date=15 October 2021 |archive-date=8 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211108232044/https://www.trouw.nl/wetenschap/van-oldenborgh-maakt-zich-geen-zorgen-over-zijn-ziekte-wel-over-het-klimaat-ik-zal-nooit-weten-hoe-dit-afloopt~b2c6f980/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Van Oldenborgh died from it on 12 October 2021, aged 59, in [[Gouda, South Holland]].<ref name="auto" /><ref name="auto2" /><ref name="auto3" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.volkskrant.nl/gs-b6b84f59 |title=Internationaal vermaarde klimaatwetenschapper Geert Jan van Oldenborgh overleden |trans-title=Internationally renowned climate scientist Geert Jan van Oldenborgh has passed away |first=Maarten|last=Keulemans |date=13 October 2021 |website=[[de Volkskrant]] |access-date=15 October 2021}}</ref><ref name="nytobit" />
